text:
marta_ops: FYI - after the 02:10 UTC kernel rollout to ap-northeast-1 GPU node pool, ~28 hosts are repeatedly failing to load the nvidia module and are cycling pods. Noticed during routine capacity warmup.
ryan_infra: digging in. can you paste the dmesg from one of the failing hosts?
marta_ops: here are the relevant lines:
```
[  215.342871] nvidia: probe of nvidia0 failed with error -517
[  215.342879] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
[  215.343110] nvhost: device fifo overflow
[  216.001002] nvlink: remote link down, retrying
[  216.108244] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000010
```
kevin_oncall: that probe error (-517) usually indicates async probe dependency / firmware or driver ABI mismatch with kernel. Do we have DKMS build logs?
sarah_platform: DKMS build failed in the node init logs for several hosts: "ERROR: modpost: symbol __tracepoint_module_set_init is unresolved" and "unsupported kernel version: 6.3.0-rc2". Looks like our image builder pulled the new kernel package accidentally.
marta_ops: we only targeted the control plane for 6.3 but the infra pipeline propagated the package to GPU pool due to tag mismatch.
leo_sre: consequences: affected nodes are flapping and being cordoned by kubelet -> evictions. We're losing ~40% of P4 capacity in ap-northeast-1; queued jobs are bouncing to other regions. Cost forecast: additional spot allocations + cross-region egress could add ~$7k/day if this persists.
jess_ml: we have long-running batch jobs stuck, training checkpoints impacted. Can we immediate cordon+drain and migrate to eu-west2? That region is near full commit, slow to spin GPUs.
ryan_infra: plan: 1) isolate affected pool: add taint gpu.k8s.redwood/unstable:NoSchedule 2) disable auto-upgrade tags in apt/repo 3) manual rollback of kernel package on a sample host to 5.15-stable and test module load 4) if rollback validated, mass rollback via image-redeploy.
kevin_oncall: manual rollback steps for a node (tested):
```
sudo apt-mark hold linux-image-6.3.* linux-headers-6.3.*
sudo apt install linux-image-5.15.0-101-generic linux-headers-5.15.0-101-generic
sudo update-grub && sudo reboot
# after reboot: sudo modprobe nvidia || journalctl -k -u nvidia-modprobe -n 200
```
ryan_infra: caveat: some hosts show DKMS never invoked because the system used vendor-compiled driver packages (non-DKMS). For those we need to redeploy vendor driver bundle compatible with 6.3 OR rollback kernel. Vendor says their 6.3 driver build is not ready.
sarah_platform: we should also check NCCL handshake logs—some pods show "NCCL WARN TCP : Allgather failed, ret=22" around the time nodes started flapping. Could be network+driver interplay when module half-inits.
leo_sre: immediate mitigating actions applied: cordoned affected nodes, turned off autoscaling for that pool to avoid churn, bumped capacity requests to other regions by 20%. Notified billing for potential overage.
jess_ml: any quick workaround that avoids mass rollback? e.g., use lightweight container runtime that bypasses driver?
kevin_oncall: no, driver load is at host level; GPU-using containers will fail without proper modules. We can try passthrough to a different instance type in same AZ (different AMI) but capacity is limited.
ryan_infra: request to oncall: approve rolling rollback to 5.15 on the GPU pool. Need sign-off because it will trigger reboots across many hosts. What are SLA tradeoffs?
kevin_oncall: approve. Schedule rolling reboot in 10-min waves: 2 nodes at a time to keep capacity. We'll monitor for OOM/kernel oops after revert. Also open provider support ticket: PV-3482 (referenced).
sarah_platform: posting commands to disable auto-upgrades in repo: `echo "APT::Periodic::Enable 0;" > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/10periodic` and remove the pipeline tag that pushed 6.3.
marta_ops: deploying rollback to a small canary (3 nodes) now. I'll update status.
deploy-bot: rollout started: 3-node canary rollback (ap-northeast-1-gpu-pool) - 1967345685
leo_sre: reminder: create follow-up playbook for kernel compatibility checks: matrix of kernel x driver x cuda x nccL x distro, and gate the image builder. This incident shows we lack the gate.
jess_ml: thanks. once canary is good we'll queue long jobs. current ETA unknown for full recovery.
ryan_infra: canary report: 2/3 nodes back online, nvidia module loads fine on 5.15, workloads resumed. One node failed to come up due to unrelated disk corruption. Proceeding with phased rollback.
kevin_oncall: keep the taint in place until pool stabilized. Also add alert rule for "nvidia module probe failures > 5 hosts in 10m".
marta_ops: incident update posted to #incidents and sent to customers in impacted tenants.
leo_sre: postmortem owners: ryan_infra + sarah_platform + marta_ops. Action items: freeze kernel upgrades to GPU pools, add DKMS/unit test in image build, add provider gate for vendor drivers, cost contingency runbook.
kevin_oncall: thanks all. tag me if any nodes re-oom or if NCCL errors persist after full rollback. :thumbsup:
